newsitem.title: UK: Belships to bid for Western Bulk.
newsitem.headline: Belships to bid for Western Bulk.

text.p: Norwegian shipping group Belships Company Ltd Ships-ASA will Monday open a cash offer for handymax bulk carrier owner and operator Western Bulk Shipping.
Belships will offer 38 Norwegian crowns ($5.02) for each Western Bulk Shipping share it does not already own, valuing the company at 517 million crowns.
The offer will be open for two weeks and a day, said Belships managing director Sverre Tidemand. Offer documentation was being sent to shareholders Friday.
Western Bulk Shipping operates one of the world's largest handymax bulk carrier pools with around 70 vessels through subsidiary Western Bulk Carriers.
Belships currently owns a 43 percent stake in Western Bulk Shipping. The two company have close historic ties. ($ = 7.568 Norwegian Crowns)

Tidemand said the offer was intended as a first step to increase the liquidity of Western Bulk Shipping shares. Belships intends to place any shares acquired through the offer with other new shareholders.
Tidemand said: "The aim is to maintain the stock market listing of Western Bulk Shipping but increase the liquidity of its shares."
Lack of liquidity is a common problem facing shipping companies listed in Oslo.

In addition to Belships' 43 percent stake, Norwegian engineering and shipbuilding group Kvaerner ASA owns 18 percent of Western Bulk Shipping and Sjoinvest 26 percent, leaving free float of around 13 percent.

Sjoinvest, owned by Norwegian shipping investor Pal Caspersen, recently increased its stake with the acquisition of a 17 per cent tranche of shares for 80 million crowns equating to 35 crowns a share.
Kvaerner has previously said it intends to progressively dispose of non-core assets. It has sold several shipping investments in recent years.
Shipping analysts in Oslo said Belships move may be linked a desire to retain control of Western Bulk Shipping.
"It looks like this is all about Belships keeping control of the company," argued a shipping analyst who declined to be named. "The question is whether and at what price Kvaerner will sell."
A Kvaerner spokeswoman in London said the company would consider the situation carefully.
"We are awaiting a written offer from Belships, and will only take a decision after that offer has been fully considered," she said.
"We cannot comment at this stage whether we feel it is good or bad, or should be higher or lower. Any other comments would be merely speculation."
Sjoinvest director Malven Kleppen said his firm thought the Belships offer too low, but had not yet taken a final decision.
"We are looking into the company seriously. It seems for us, however, that 38 crowns is just too low," he said.
Tidemand is also chairman of dry bulk shipowner association Intercargo.
